---
name: prioritize
description: Rank the issues waiting in the Triage column by dependencies, value and size, set Priority, Size and Estimate, and move them to Todo in execution order, explaining the order in an issue comment. Use when issues in Triage need to be ordered and handed to the coder, or when asked to prioritize, order or queue the backlog.

# Prioritize

Turns the Triage column into an ordered Todo queue. Reads the dependencies from the issue **Relationships** (blocked by / blocking), never from the issue text. Reuses `/triage` for labels and agent briefs; does not duplicate it.

Every comment posted must start with: `> *This was generated by AI during triage.*`

## 1. Read the queue

```bash
~/.claude/skills/prioritize/scripts/queue.sh
```

JSON with `board` and `issues` (number, title, labels, `hasAcceptance`, `blockedBy` with each blocker's `state` and board `status`, `blocking`). With a board these are the issues in Triage; with no board (`board: null`) all open issues. Read an issue (`gh issue view <n>`) when title and labels are not enough to judge value and size.

## 2. Check readiness

An issue is **ready** when it has a clear description and acceptance criteria (`hasAcceptance`) and no `needs-info`, `wontfix` or `dup` label. Not ready: leave it in Triage, comment what is missing, name `/triage` as the way to resolve it. Size XL: leave it in Triage and recommend splitting it with `/to-issues`.

## 3. Set Priority, Size, Estimate

| Priority | Meaning |
|---|---|
| P0 | Fixes something broken, or other queued issues are blocked by it |
| P1 | Normal planned work |
| P2 | Nice to have, nobody waits for it |

| Size | Effort | Estimate (hours) |
|---|---|---|
| XS | under 1 hour | 1 |
| S | up to half a day | 3 |
| M | about a day | 6 |
| L | 2-3 days | 16 |
| XL | more | split it, do not queue |

## 4. Order

1. A blocker is **settled** when it is closed, or its board column is Todo, Doing, Review or Testing, or it is ranked earlier in this run.
2. An issue may be queued only when all its blockers are settled. A blocker that is itself not ready keeps its dependents in Triage. A cycle: queue none of it and report it.
3. Among the issues that may be queued, pick by: higher Priority, then the one that blocks more issues, then smaller Size, then lower number. Repeat until none is left.

## 5. Apply in order, one issue at a time

```bash
B=~/.claude/skills/project-board/scripts/board.sh
$B claim <n> triager
$B set <n> Priority P1 ; $B set <n> Size M ; $B set <n> Estimate 6
$B move <n> todo        # also clears the Agent field
```

Move the highest-ranked issue first; the column keeps that order. Then comment on each issue: its place in the queue (`#k of N`), Priority and Size with a one-line reason, and its blockers.

## No board

The same commands run and print `SKIPPED` for the board parts. Do the ranking and relationship checks, set nothing, move nothing, and post the proposed order as a comment on each issue and as a summary to the user. The handover is manual.

## Report

End with a table: order, issue, Priority, Size, and for every issue left in Triage the reason.
